//: Captions, theme and order for `appshot compose`. Text, so marketing copy changes without touching code or re-capturing. See the `screenshots-*` targets in the root Makefile.
//output: The Mac App Store's 16:10 canvas. Cupertino does not ship on the App Store — docs/distribution.md settles that — but this is still the right size: it is the one shape the compositor accepts, it is what a README, a Product Hunt gallery and an OG card all want, and it means the framed set is upload-ready if that decision is ever revisited. DemoSeed pins the window to 1120x700, the same 1.6:1, so the capture fills the width without letterboxing.
//appearances: Dark only, on purpose. apps/website/src/styles/global.css: "Dark is the base, not an override... there is no light theme to be faithful to and none is invented here." Capturing light too would double the run and commit three goldens that nothing renders and nobody reviews. Adding "light" here and to the Makefile's APPEARANCES is the whole change if the site ever grows one.
//fontFamily: SF Pro Display is NOT part of a stock macOS install — it ships in Apple's SF font pack. `make screenshots-doctor` refuses to compose if it does not resolve, which is the only way to catch a silent substitution.
fontFamily: 'SF Pro Display', -apple-system, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
//themes: "Horizon": the mark's own composition rather than a quotation of its colours. Cupertino is a low sun over two hills, so the warmth is a floor under the window and the ink is above the title, where the type needs it. Still not a second palette — apps/website/src/styles/global.css is the one that exists, and a store image in colours the site does not use reads as a different product.
//angle: 270 = bottom-up. Degrees CLOCKWISE, y-DOWN, and appshot means it literally: offset 0 lands where the axis starts, so at 270 that is the bottom edge. The old JS compositor fed the angle through an SVG gradientTransform in objectBoundingBox units and then skewed it by the canvas aspect ratio, which is why the 145 that used to be here rendered at about 135. Do not port an angle from that era without re-rendering it.
//floor: The warm floor and the window's drop shadow (layout.shadow: blur 52, opacity 0.34) occupy the same band, so #8A4A2E is chosen to sit under the shadow rather than compete with it. Lifting it toward the accent's own #F2895C is what makes the shadow read as dirt. The 0.24 stop is what keeps it a floor instead of a wash.
//screens: Order here IS the order of the framed set — it stamps the 01-, 02- prefix. The capture filenames stay unnumbered, so reordering never renames an image. `id` matches <id>~dark.png in source/, and it is also the -ScreenshotStage value DemoSeed.Stage parses.
//website: The basename `appshot compose website` writes into apps/website/src/assets/shots/. All five are on the site. `prompt` and `activity` are the same Log pane and they earn separate slots only because their fixtures differ — one question's trace, then the general log with a refusal in it. Caption them so that difference is the point; captioned loosely they read as the same picture twice.

screens.//: The title used to open with a literal "Four", which Contacts invalidated the day it shipped — the same drift apps/website/src/config.ts exists to prevent, in the one file that cannot compute a count. It no longer states one. The subtitle still names the surfaces because a caption that will not say which apps is not worth the plate; Messages, Safari and Maps then landed without it being revisited, and it named five surfaces out of eight until the sidebar grew a dimmed row and somebody looked again.
screens.title: Your Apple apps. One permission.
screens.subtitle: Mail, Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Messages, Safari and Maps, brokered by a single signed app. Switch off the ones you do not use.

screens.//: Captioned with the prompt itself, which is why `prompt` is its own stage rather than a second crop of `activity`: DemoSeed.heroTurnLogLines seeds this pane with that one question's trace and nothing else. The subtitle is HERO_TURN.prompt in apps/website/src/data/examples.ts, verbatim — that file is the authority, the site checks its own half at build time, and nothing yet checks this copy of it.
screens.title: Ask in plain English.
screens.subtitle: “What did I promise Marie last week, and is any of it on my calendar?”

screens.title: You can watch it the whole time.
screens.subtitle: Every tool call, live — tool names only, never your content.

screens.title: Every client. Every session.
screens.subtitle: See exactly what is connected, and what it has asked for.

screens.//: Claude Code's CLIENT pane, in the main window. This has now been three different screens under one stage id: the Permissions form, then the Clients settings pane, now a client detail pane in the sidebar. The id has never followed, and for the reason it did not follow the last time — renaming a stage touches SHOT_SCREENS, three golden filenames, two appstore prefixes and an Astro import, and mixing that with a UI change makes the golden diff unreadable. DemoSeed no longer orders the main window out for this stage, since this IS the main window; `Subject.settings` is kept for the next pane that outgrows a form. What is on screen is read from DemoSeed.clientConfig rather than from the capturing Mac, because the real file is full of the developer's own servers and folders.
screens.title: Wired into your editor, not inside it.
screens.subtitle: One click to configure a client — and the file it writes, shown in full: every key, where it points, and what Cupertino leaves alone.

screens.//: Deliberately the same window and layout as `surface`, and the pair is the point: `surface` is Mail with writes ON and its full tool list, this is Notes with writes OFF and a visibly shorter one. The write gate used to be photographed as a row of toggles in Settings, which pictured the control; this pictures the consequence, which is what the caption claims. The numbers are read off the real server by CapabilitiesCard rather than seeded, so if writes-off ever stopped shrinking the list this plate would say so.
screens.title: Writes are off until you say so.
screens.subtitle: With the toggle off, the mutating tools are never registered — seven tools here against Mail's twenty. An assistant is not refused; it is never told they exist.
